_comment: The status-aware stack map. Ruled 2026-09-11 (ruling 3): keep the diagram, but give every component its own DERIVED status — the fault was false aggregation, not diagrams. MAP1-MAP5 in build.mjs enforce it; prove-gate.mjs proves each refuses for its own reason.
_why_edges_are_data: Per-node status alone does not close the SCOPE problem, because in a stack diagram the overclaim lives in the CONNECTOR, not the label. A node marked `draft` still reads load-bearing if a solid arrow runs through it. So an edge names its endpoints and, if it has one, its integration witness — and the state it is drawn in is derived from what is actually there. See edge_states.
_what_a_path_proves: CORRECTED 2026-09-12. The first version drew an edge SOLID when both endpoint paths existed, and called that witnessed. Two files existing does not witness a connection between them — that is the same overclaim MAP4 was invented to catch, one level up. There are now THREE states and only an executable integration witness earns the strongest one.

gates.MAP1: a node rendered without a derived status chip and without a status_why saying why it has none → refused
gates.MAP2: a status token not in protocols.json's own vocabulary → refused
gates.MAP3: a hand-written node status — derived or absent, the same rule as surface_rung → refused
gates.MAP4: the page drawing an edge in a state the record does not earn. THREE states: solid needs an executable integration witness covering both endpoints; dashed means both endpoints exist and nothing exercised the connection; missing means an endpoint is absent. A declared integration that does not cover both endpoints, names a path that is not there, or cites a failing run, is refused outright
gates.MAP5: a protocol in protocols.json that no node accounts for → refused. Added during implementation: the hand-written diagram this replaces covered ten of the twelve protocols and silently omitted OS-011 and OS-012
gates.MAP6: edge language claiming witness, verification or proof where it is not earned — checked on the edges_heading AND on every edge_states entry other than `solid`, in the record and again on the emitted page. Mere path existence may not be called witnessed

edge_states._comment: MAP6 refuses any state other than `solid` whose `means` uses the language of witness, verification or proof. The legend is data so the page cannot drift from the rule.

solid.label: integration has run
solid.means: an executable test or a generated receipt names and exercises both endpoints, and it passed

dashed.label: available, unverified
dashed.means: both endpoints exist and nothing has exercised the connection between them

missing.label: endpoint absent
missing.means: one or both endpoints do not exist

_integration_shape: An edge may declare integration: {kind: 'receipt'|'test', path, exercises: [...], cmd?}. `exercises` must cover BOTH endpoint paths or MAP4 refuses the record rather than quietly downgrading it. For kind 'receipt' the file must be a run receipt whose execution_identity.exit is 0 — a failing run may not be cited as an integration. Nothing in this stack declares one today, so every edge below is dashed or missing and none is solid.
edges_heading: What connects them, and what has actually been run
_edges_heading_comment: MAP6 covers this too. It read 'what witnesses the connection' while sitting directly above four edges that nothing has exercised — the heading asserting for the whole list what only one state earns. The legend rows were gated and the heading above them was not.
